title: China Shipping: Transpacific Rates Drop as Demand Cools
metaDescription: Transpacific spot rates fall as peak season ends. ZIM launches new express service from Shanghai and Xiamen to LA. Red Sea routing returns.
bottomLine: Shanghai to Los Angeles spot rates fell 6% to $7,514 per 40ft as peak demand flatlines. Carriers are pushing November rate hikes, but the market is resisting.

stories.headline: Transpacific spot rates drop as peak season ends
stories.tldr: Shanghai to Los Angeles spot rates fell 6% to $7,514 per 40ft in the week ending 30 October 2026.
stories.whatHappened:
Drewry recorded the steepest one-week fall in transpacific eastbound spot rates since June 2025. The Shanghai-Los Angeles route declined 6% to $7,514 per 40ft, while the Shanghai-New York route fell 5% to $9,631 per 40ft.

Carriers are attempting to implement rate hikes for November. However, analysts suggest these hikes are doomed because demand has gone flat following a protracted peak season.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you are booking spot freight for November or December, you have the leverage. Carriers want higher prices, but the data shows the market is cooling. You should push back on any General Rate Increases (GRIs) your forwarder tries to apply this week.

For sellers with high-volume shipments, the gap between New York and Los Angeles rates remains wide. If your US distribution allows it, routing to the West Coast and using rail is currently a significant cost saver compared to the East Coast. This shift protects your margin during the final holiday push.
stories.hotTake: Carriers always try to hike rates at the start of the month. This time they are fighting a dead market. Do not pay the November GRI. Hold your ground and wait for the discounted offers that forwarders are already reporting.
actions: Reject any November GRI requests from your freight forwarder
Quote multiple providers for spot rates to capture the 5-6% slide
Shift urgent late-Q4 volume to West Coast ports to save on freight

stories.headline: ZIM launches 12-day express service from Shanghai to LA
stories.tldr: ZIM starts the ZX3 service in December 2026, offering a 12-day transit from Shanghai to Los Angeles.
stories.whatHappened:
ZIM is launching the ZX3 premium expedited service in December 2026. The rotation connects Xiamen and Shanghai directly to Los Angeles. It provides a 12-day transit from Shanghai and a 15-day transit from Xiamen.

The service includes berth on arrival in China and a dedicated berth at the WBCT terminal in Los Angeles. Cargo is discharged onto ZIM-dedicated chassis for immediate availability without appointments. The service also provides expedited rail connections to Chicago, New York, Memphis, Dallas, and Kansas City.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you are fighting a stockout for the December holidays, this is your escape valve. A 12-day transit from Shanghai to LA is aggressive. It removes the usual dwell time and appointment queues at the terminal, which usually kill your lead time and leave goods stranded on the quay.

You will pay a premium for this. But for high-margin goods or critical replenishment, the cost of the premium service is lower than the cost of an empty shelf during the final two weeks of the year. This is a tactical move for high-value SKUs that cannot wait for standard transit.
stories.hotTake: Most sellers overpay for 'express' services that still get stuck in port queues. ZIM is actually solving the bottleneck here with dedicated chassis and no-appointment pickups. That is where the real value is, not the sailing speed.
actions: Check ZX3 availability for your December replenishment
Compare the total lead time of ZX3 against your current carrier's 'express' option
Route urgent Xiamen-sourced stock through this service to hit the 15-day window

stories.headline: Red Sea returns create port bunching and rate volatility
stories.tldr: 63% of Asia-Europe capacity is routing through the Red Sea again, causing ships to bunch at destination ports.
stories.whatHappened:
Carriers are returning to the Red Sea to shorten schedules. Alphaliner reports that 24 of 46 direct services between Asia and Europe now use the passage, representing 63% of deployed capacity. Mediterranean routes have a higher return rate at 70% compared to 58% for North Europe.

Zim has returned to the Red Sea for its joint Asia-US East Coast service with MSC. This shift is causing ships to arrive ahead of schedules that were built for longer Africa voyages, leading to vessel bunching at terminals.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship to Europe, your transit times are shrinking, but your port dwell times may increase. When ships bunch together, terminals clog. You might see your ship arrive early only for your container to sit on the quay for an extra week because the terminal is overwhelmed.

This volatility is keeping rates higher than demand justifies. Asia-North Europe rates rose 3% to $3,551 per FEU, and Mediterranean rates rose 8% to $4,252 per FEU in the last week. You are paying for congestion and carrier capacity restrictions, not for a genuine lack of space on ships.
stories.hotTake: The return to the Red Sea is a gamble by carriers to cut costs. They are trading a long, predictable route around Africa for a shorter, volatile route. Expect schedule slides and terminal chaos in Europe for the next month.
actions: Add five days of buffer to your European inland delivery estimates
Check with your EU customs broker for increased dwell times at Mediterranean ports
Avoid booking 'just in time' for European warehouse arrivals

stories.headline: Maersk adds reefer surcharge for shipments to Ghana
stories.tldr: Maersk introduces a Peak Season Surcharge for refrigerated cargo to Tema, Ghana, effective 16 November 2026.
stories.whatHappened:
Maersk will introduce a Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) for refrigerated cargo moving from the Far East, Middle East, and Americas to Tema, Ghana. The surcharge takes effect on 16 November 2026 for most regions.

For regulated countries, the surcharge will apply from 1 December 2026. This fee targets 20-foot and 40-foot reefer containers specifically on the route to Tema.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship temperature-controlled goods to West Africa, your landed cost is about to rise. This is a targeted surcharge on reefers, meaning your standard dry containers are unaffected, but your perishables or chemicals are hit.

You need to check if your current contracts protect you from PSS or if you are on a spot rate. If you are on spot, you must account for this fee in your pricing for any shipments departing after 16 November. It is a small lane, but the cost per unit on reefers can spike quickly with these adders.
stories.hotTake: Maersk is testing the waters on niche lanes. They know reefer cargo has fewer alternatives than dry cargo. If you have a choice, look for carriers that haven't slapped a PSS on the Ghana route yet.
actions: Audit all refrigerated shipments bound for Tema departing after 16 November
Update your landed cost calculations for West African reefer cargo
Request a fixed rate from alternative carriers to avoid the PSS

contentHooks: Stop paying November GRIs when transpacific spot rates are sliding 6%.
The real bottleneck in shipping isn't the ocean, it's the terminal appointment queue.
ZIM's new 12-day transit is a lifeline for Q4 stockouts if you have the margin.
Red Sea returns are shortening voyages but lengthening port dwell times in Europe.
Sellers are paying a 'congestion tax' on Asia-Europe lanes despite cooling demand.
If you can route to LA and rail to the East Coast, do it now to beat NY rates.
Carrier rate hikes in November are a bluff. The data shows demand is flat.
Dedicated chassis are the only way to guarantee your goods leave the port on time.
The gap between Shanghai-LA and Shanghai-NY rates is a strategic lever for US sellers.
Don't mistake a shorter sailing time for a faster delivery if the port is bunched.

faq.question: Are ocean freight rates from China to the US falling?
faq.answer: Yes. Spot rates on the Shanghai to Los Angeles route fell 6% to $7,514 per 40ft, and Shanghai to New York fell 5% to $9,631 per 40ft in the week ending 30 October 2026. This follows the end of the peak shipping season and a flattening of US import demand.

faq.question: How can I get goods to the US faster in December?
faq.answer: ZIM is launching the ZX3 service in December 2026. It offers a direct 12-day transit from Shanghai to Los Angeles and 15 days from Xiamen to Los Angeles. It uses dedicated berths and chassis at the WBCT terminal in LA to avoid appointment queues, which significantly speeds up the final leg of delivery.

faq.question: Why are Asia-Europe rates rising if demand is cooling?
faq.answer: Rates are being supported by port congestion and carriers using blank sailings to restrict capacity. Additionally, the return of 63% of capacity to the Red Sea route is causing ships to arrive in bunches, putting pressure on terminals and keeping prices higher than they would be in a fluid market.

faq.question: Is there a new surcharge for shipping to Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. Maersk is introducing a Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) for refrigerated cargo moving from the Far East, Middle East, and Americas to Tema, Ghana. This takes effect on 16 November 2026, or 1 December 2026 for regulated countries.
